claims.text: The initial HfNbTaTiZr alloy contains inherent nanoscale compositional fluctuations.
Nanoscale compositional heterogeneities govern the anomalous stress–strain and thermoelastic behavior of HfNbTaTiZr.
Nanoscale compositional heterogeneities produce mismatches in local thermal expansion.
Local thermal-expansion mismatches generate internal stresses during temperature changes.
The resulting internal thermal stresses influence dislocation mobility.
The resulting internal thermal stresses influence phase evolution or phase stability.
Internal thermal stresses enhance creep at high temperature.
Internal thermal stresses modify work hardening after cold rolling and aging.
Internal thermal stresses affect measured elastic moduli by altering lattice strains.
Controlled homogenization or annealing will reduce nanoscale compositional heterogeneity.
Reducing compositional heterogeneity will lower local thermal-expansion mismatch and internal thermal stress.
Homogenized samples will have lower creep strain rates at 1250 °C than untreated samples.
Homogenization will modify microhardness evolution during cold working and aging at 600–800 °C.
Homogenized samples will exhibit more conventional elastic-modulus trends than untreated samples.
Untreated samples with greater compositional fluctuations will retain higher internal stresses and the anomalous behavior.
Phase stability is maintained over the proposed testing range extending to 1250 °C.

contradictions.description: The initial state is described as either as-cast or homogenized, but homogenization is also the intervention intended to distinguish treated samples from a baseline explicitly defined as having no homogenization treatment.
